standard-dialogue.npc: Greetings traveller. Welcome to 'The Hair Of The Dog' Tavern. What can I do you for?

steps.npc: Well that's my speciality! The local brew's named 'Moonlight Mead' and will set you back 5 gold. Whaddya say? Fancy a pint?

steps.text: If the player doesn't have enough coins:

steps.player: I don't have the money on me right now though... can I start a tab?

steps.npc: You see that sign behind me there?

steps.player: The one that says; 'Please Do Not Ask For Credit As Being Attacked By A Large Angry Werewolf Inn Keeper Often Offends'?

steps.npc: Bingo.

steps.text: If the player has enough coins:

steps.npc: Here ya go pal. Enjoy!
Eh, suit yourself. You're missing out on a genuine taste experience.
Well, I dunno... The village is kind of on the fringe out here, I dunno how up to date the stuff I hear about is...
You want to know about Canifis? I dunno why, not a lot happens here. We're just your typical everyday down at earth werewolf folk, after all...

steps.player: So... everyone here is a werewolf?

steps.npc: Yep. We are as Zamorak made us!
Yeah, he's great isn't he? Every year we hold a big festival to give thanks to Zamorak for keeping us well fed and happy here.
I hear over in the West they worship Saradomin, but I dunno why! What's he ever done to help out us werewolves, huh?
I hear he has all these crazy followers who say things like we shouldn't kill people and eat them! What's up with that?
Aaaah, not for a good few months yet. Come and ask me again nearer to the time, I'll keep some extra meat and mead back from the rest for ya pal.

options.text: Tell me about the land of Morytania.

steps.player: Tell me about the land of Morytania.

steps.npc: Well, I don't know what to tell you really... This village is called Canifis and lies on the border between Morytania and Misthalin... so we're kind of on the front line if those Saradominists to the west ever decide to
attack us...
No? The Saradominists hate us. It's only thanks to Lord Drakan that these lands are kept safe.
Ahhh... you must be new to these parts if you haven't heard of Lord Drakan! He's the lord of this land, and we all pledge allegiance to him.
In return for our allegiance, and the tithe of course, he keeps our land safe from any invaders and the Saradominists who want to kill us all.

Ah, well, in return for his protection, we have to give Lord Drakan a share of blood every week. If we don't have any to spare from our hunts, then we need to pick a member of the village to give their life in return
for the blood so that the tithe is fulfilled.

steps.player: You mean you kill someone you know in order to meet the tithe???

steps.npc: That's right, but only if we haven't managed to get enough spare blood from our hunts. It's kind of severe if you look at it that way, but frankly, I think the price is fair in return for his protection and his tolerance of
our village. He could probably kill us all if he wanted us gone, so keeping on his good side is worth the sacrifice to us. Lucky we're not human really!
He hates humans! Apparently long ago his brother Draynor was trapped in Misthalin and lost much of his powers, and was recently killed by some human!

steps.text: If Vampyre Slayer is not completed:

steps.npc: He hates humans! Apparently his brother Draynor is trapped in Misthalin, and adventurous little human wannabe-heroes keep trying to kill him!
Man, I'd hate to be a human around here, that's for sure. Drakan would really enjoy hunting them down and killing them!

Well, I don't know what to tell you really... This village is called Canifis and lies on the border between Morytania and Misthalin... so we're kind of on the front line if those Saradominists to the west ever decide to
attack us...

No? The Saradominists hate us. It was only thanks to Lord Drakan that these lands were kept safe, but now he's gone and we've got some new overlord who apparently wants us to all be friends! Like that's ever
going to happen!

steps.player: So... Are you going to do something about that?

steps.npc: Me? Of course not! Someone really should though...

options.text: Tell me about the shopkeepers here.

steps.player: Tell me about the shopkeepers here.

steps.npc: Hmmm? Why, who did you want to hear the gossip about?

steps.player: Tell me what you know about Sbott the Tanner.

steps.npc: Hey, I won't hear a word said bad about that guy! He's an honest and hard-working wolf if I ever met one! He charges a lot for his job, but he's one of the best tanners I've ever seen - and I'm over four hundred
years old! You need stuff tanning, I recommend him!

steps.player: Know anything interesting about Rufus the food seller?

steps.npc: Ah yeah... good old Rufus... He's kind of getting on in years and doesn't like to come out of his wolf form so often, but let me tell you this: that guy is a hunter through and through. You seen how much food he

catches a day? That takes real dedication! Some of the young pups think just because a wolf has a bit of grey in his fur then he's past it, but I've seen him put those pups to shame in a hunt! He's a real inspiration to us
all!

steps.player: Got anything to share about Barker the clothes seller?

steps.npc: Eh, I don't like the guy much, but you can't knock the quality of his stock. They're some fine quality threads you can get yourself there.
Eh... I can't really tell you to be honest. Something about the guy just gets my hackles up everytime he opens his yap, know what I mean?
Lucky for you. I can't really explain it, I just don't like the guy. Does great clothes though, you got to give him that.

steps.player: I bet you have some juicy gossip about Fidelio the general store owner.

steps.npc: That nut job? Oh sure, we all know about him. He was a real firebrand daredevil when he was younger, always taking risks to make himself a quick buck... he got himself caught up in the smuggling trade, sneaking over
the border into Misthalin and pretending to be a human so he could buy exotic items to sell.

steps.player: Exotic items? From Misthalin? Like what?

steps.npc: Oh man, you name it! Flour... buckets... tinderboxes... chisels... he could get the lot! He's been doing it so long now though, his nerves are shot.
Nowadays he's a disgrace, he can barely string a sentence together and jumps at his own shadow. Makes you feel ashamed to be a werewolf.

options.text: Tell me about the temple to the West.

steps.player: Tell me about the temple to the west.

steps.npc: Well, I'm not old enough to remember the full story behind it, but it was a terrible day for these lands when it was built there.
Apparently, Morytania was once a strong and mighty kingdom, with lands spreading far further west than they do today, and south into the desert as well.

That was all until the day when a sneak attack by the hated human forces who worship Saradomin burned our villages and slaughtered our peoples in mass. To rub salt into the wound, they then cursed the river as well!
Luckily they seem to have calmed down somewhat recently, and tend to stay on their side of the river... but the wrong they have done my people will never be forgotten, and will never be forgiven!
Absolutely! If I ever met one I would gobble him up where he stands! And then chew the bones for dessert!
A story??? Heh, well the only one I can think of right now is one my dear old mammy told me as a pup...
Now how did it go... Ah yes!

Once upon a time a brave young wolf was walking through a forest, when he came upon a human dressed all in red. 'Aha!' he thought to himself, 'Here's a nice easy meal!' But the human talked to him, and as he was
always taught to be a polite wolf, he spoke back to it.

Well, this cunning human told him that there was a better meal that would not run away in a house in the woods. As the brave young wolf could see that this human was not fully grown, he figured maybe he'd

better get a better meal at this house, so he ran as fast as his paws could carry him to the house the human told him about... inside he found an old human lying in bed, and although the meat was a little tough, as the

human was older than he thought, he had a good meal and decided to sleep it off in the house for awhile. He had not been asleep long though, when he was woken by a knocking at the door. The human in red had followed

him to the house! Suspecting a human trap, the brave young wolf put on the old humans clothes and jumped into the bed, so that he could pretend to be human and escape from this terrible trap! Well now, this human

dressed in red came into the house, and pretended to believe the brave wolf was really a human, and began to talk to him. But then the human started asking strange questions of the wolf, because the human knew that it

was not a human at all! The brave young wolf decided to try and escape, for it was only a young human, and not very strong, so the brave young wolf said he would eat the human if they did not let him escape! As he said

this however, the human in red shouted out at him: 'Aha! You are a wolf!' and as the human shouted this another bigger human ran into the room from outside! This bigger human was much stronger and was
carrying an axe, and the poor young wolf died in this terrible trap made for him by the humans.
And do you know what the moral of this story is?
It's 'Never trust humans' of course! My dear old mammy told me that story when I was a pup, and I'm still alive and well to tell it to you today!
Pretty good story huh?

steps.player: Um... yeah. It was great. Really.

steps.npc: ...I don't know why you talked to me if you don't want anything then...

treasure-trails-medium.text: Roavar has given you another clue scroll!
